stem: Iron pyrite, $\text{FeS}_2$, has a yellow colour that makes it look like gold metal. The compound contains the ions $\text{Fe}^{2+}$ and $\text{S}_2^{2-}$.

parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.text: Give the full electronic configuration of $\text{Fe}^{2+}$.

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.text:
Calculate the oxidation number of sulfur in the $\text{S}_2^{2-}$ ion.
Assume that each sulfur atom in the ion has the same oxidation number.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Describe the metallic bonding in gold.

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.stem:
Iron pyrite is often called fool's gold because of its appearance. Impure samples of iron pyrite often contain a small amount of gold.

The gold can be obtained from impure iron pyrite. The impure iron pyrite is roasted in oxygen, to produce iron(III) oxide and sulfur dioxide. Gold does not react with oxygen.
parts.text:
The sulfur dioxide produced during roasting would cause environmental consequences if released into the atmosphere.

State and explain **one** of these environmental consequences.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text:
Complete the equation to show the roasting of iron pyrite in oxygen.

$$4\text{FeS}_2 + \text{          } \rightarrow 2\text{Fe}_2\text{O}_3 + \text{          }$$

parts.label: (c)(iii)
parts.text:
A sample of impure iron pyrite was roasted in oxygen. The composition of the mixture of solid products is shown.

| solid product | mass/g |
| :--- | :--- |
| $\text{Fe}_2\text{O}_3$ | 33.18 |
| $\text{Au}$ | 0.37 |

Calculate the mass of $\text{FeS}_2$ present in the sample of impure iron pyrite.
Assume that all the $\text{FeS}_2$ was converted to $\text{Fe}_2\text{O}_3$ during the roasting process.

($M_{\text{r}}$: $\text{FeS}_2$, 120.0; $\text{Fe}_2\text{O}_3$, 159.6)

parts.label: (c)(iv)
parts.text:
Use your answer to **(iii)** to calculate the percentage by mass of gold in this sample of impure iron pyrite. Assume that gold is the only impurity in this sample of impure iron pyrite.

Give your answer to **two** significant figures.

(If you were unable to calculate an answer to **(iii)**, use 55.00 g as the mass of $\text{FeS}_2$ in this calculation. This is **not** the correct answer.)
